transition.event: Alexander the Great conquers the Achaemenid Persian Empire
transition.ref_note: Daniel 8:5,20-21 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the he-goat 'from the west' (v.5), self-interpreted in the text as Grecia overthrowing Media-Persia (vv.20-21); traditionally dated 334-330 BC -- see egypt.toml's own mirrored transition for the same conquest's reach into Egypt

fall.event: Alexander dies; his empire divides among four successor kingdoms
fall.ref_note: Daniel 8:8,22 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the he-goat's great horn 'broken,' replaced by 'four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven' (v.8), self-interpreted a few verses later as 'four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation' (v.22); traditionally dated to Alexander's 323 BC death -- see this era's own rise-transition for the same vision's earlier verses

transition.event: The Neo-Assyrian resurgence begins under Adad-nirari II
transition.ref_note: general Assyriological knowledge (the 10th-9th century BC resurgence that becomes the Neo-Assyrian Empire); no specific source consulted this session; not scripture-narrated at this specific boundary -- the KJV text's own Assyria narrative picks up later, once the empire already presses on Israel (e.g. 2 Kings 15:19)

fall.event: The Medes and Neo-Babylonians destroy Nineveh
fall.ref_note: Nahum 3:18-19 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the whole book of Nahum is a prophecy of Nineveh's own destruction, traditionally dated 612 BC; these closing verses address the king of Assyria's own ruin directly

transition.event: Nabopolassar revolts against Assyria, founding the Neo-Babylonian dynasty
transition.ref_note: general historical knowledge (Nabopolassar's own 626 BC revolt, allied with the Medes, that leads to Nineveh's fall -- see assyria.toml's own fall); no specific source consulted this session; Nabopolassar himself is not named in the KJV text

fall.event: Babylon falls; Belshazzar is slain in the night
fall.ref_note: Daniel 5:30-31 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- 'In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain... And Darius the Median took the kingdom,' traditionally dated 539 BC -- see persia.toml's own mirrored rise-transition

transition.event: The Hyksos are expelled; the New Kingdom and the Egyptian Empire begin
transition.ref_note: general Egyptological knowledge (Ahmose I's expulsion of the Hyksos, founding the 18th Dynasty); no specific source consulted this session; not otherwise scripture-narrated at this specific boundary

transition.event: The New Kingdom collapses; Egypt contracts back to the Nile valley
transition.ref_note: general Egyptological knowledge (the Late Bronze Age Collapse; Ramesses XI's own weak final reign ending the Empire); no specific source consulted this session; not otherwise scripture-narrated

transition.event: Alexander the Great conquers Egypt, ending Persian rule
transition.ref_note: Daniel 8:20-21 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Daniel's own vision, self-interpreted in the text as Media-Persia (the ram) overthrown by Grecia (the goat); Egypt was a Persian satrapy at the time (persia.toml), so this same prophecy applies here as it does to Persia's own fall/alexander-empire.toml's own rise

fall.event: Rome annexes Egypt after Actium; Cleopatra dies
fall.ref_note: general Roman/Ptolemaic history (Battle of Actium and its aftermath, 31-30 BC); no specific source consulted this session; not scripture-narrated -- this era predates the Gospel narrative entirely

transition.event: David is anointed king over all Israel
transition.ref_note: 2 Samuel 5:1,3 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- all the tribes come to David at Hebron and anoint him king over Israel, the moment this era's own name ("United Monarchy") describes

transition.event: The kingdom divides; Jeroboam is made king over Israel
transition.ref_note: 1 Kings 12:16,20 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Israel rejects Rehoboam ('to your tents, O Israel') and makes Jeroboam king; Judah alone follows the house of David (see judah.toml's own mirrored transition)

fall.ref_note: 2 Kings 17:6,23 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- fall of Samaria and the deportation to Assyria, traditionally dated 722 BC

transition.event: The kingdom divides; Judah alone follows the house of David
transition.ref_note: 1 Kings 12:16,19 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Israel rejects Rehoboam and rebels 'against the house of David unto this day'; Judah (this polity) is what remains loyal to it -- see israel.toml's own mirrored transition

transition.event: Cyrus decrees the return from exile and the rebuilding of the temple
transition.ref_note: Ezra 1:1-3 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Cyrus's own proclamation, traditionally dated 538 BC; the destruction that precedes this gap is Judah's OWN previous era's own end (2 Kings 25, not separately cited here since it falls chronologically inside the gap between these two eras, not at either one's own boundary)

transition.event: The Maccabean Revolt overthrows Seleucid rule in Judea
transition.ref_note: the revolt itself (167-160 BC) is narrated in 1 Maccabees, outside the KJV's 66-book canon -- not otherwise cited here; Daniel 11:31 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) is the prophecy traditionally read as depicting Antiochus IV's own desecration of the temple, the revolt's proximate trigger -- a prophetic application, not a narrative citation, disclosed as such

transition.event: Rome installs Herod the Great as king of Judea
transition.ref_note: Josephus (Antiquities 14/Jewish War 1), general history -- not narrated in the KJV text, which first names Herod near his own death (Matthew 2); no verse cited rather than an invented one

fall.event: Herod the Great dies; his kingdom is partitioned among his sons
fall.ref_note: Matthew 2:19 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- 'when Herod was dead'; the partition itself (Matthew 2:22's own Archelaus reigning 'in the room of his father Herod') is general history/Josephus for the specific three-way split, traditionally dated 4 BC

transition.event: Cyrus conquers Babylon, founding the Achaemenid Persian Empire
transition.ref_note: Isaiah 44:28, 45:1 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Isaiah names Cyrus by name as the Lord's own 'anointed,' generations before his reign; the conquest itself is narrated in Daniel 5 (see babylon.toml's own mirrored fall-transition), traditionally dated 539 BC

fall.event: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Tyre; Neo-Babylonian then Persian rule absorbs the coast
fall.ref_note: Ezekiel 26:3-4,7 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the Lord's own oracle against Tyre, naming 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' directly (v.7); the historical thirteen-year siege and the coast's later absorption into Persian control are general history beyond what these verses themselves narrate

transition.event: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium; the Senate names him Augustus
transition.ref_note: Actium (31 BC) and the Senate's own grant of the Augustus title (27 BC) are general Roman history -- not narrated or prophesied anywhere in the KJV text at this specific boundary; no verse cited rather than one (Luke 2:1's own later, unrelated census reference) that would risk reading as though it narrated this event under a THE SCRIPTURES heading

transition.event: Parthian and Armenian conquests reduce the Seleucid realm to a rump state
transition.ref_note: general Hellenistic-era historical knowledge (Parthia's own mid-2nd-century BC eastward conquests under Mithridates I; Tigranes of Armenia's own later inroads); no specific source consulted this session; not scripture-narrated

fall.event: Pompey annexes Syria as a Roman province, ending Seleucid rule
fall.ref_note: general Roman/Hellenistic historical knowledge (Pompey's own 64/63 BC settlement of the East); no specific source consulted this session; 1 Maccabees, the fullest narrative source for the Seleucid decline, is outside the KJV's 66-book canon
